title: A single pump
goals: Name a basic event and give it a probability between 0 and 1.
Make that event the top event and read the result.
assumptions: The probability 0.1 is made up for teaching. It describes no real pump and says nothing about any plant.

steps.prompt: Add one basic event and name it P, for "Pump P fails".
steps.hint: Use the Basic event button. Then select the event, open the Properties tab and type P in the Name field. The lesson finds your events by their names.

steps.prompt: Give P a probability of 0.1. Write it as a fraction of 1, so 10 percent is 0.1.
steps.hint: Probabilities run from 0 to 1. 0.1 means one chance in ten.

steps.prompt: Make P the top event "No coolant flow", then run the analysis.
steps.hint: With one pump and no other way to lose flow, the pump failing is the top event.

mistakes.message: A probability of 10 is not allowed. Probabilities are between 0 and 1, so 10 percent is written 0.1.
A gate with one input only repeats that input. Use the event itself as the top event.
An event that no gate uses and that is not the top event does not affect the result.

hand_calculation: There is one way to lose flow: the pump fails.
Top event probability = P(P) = 0.1. The only cut set is {P}.
